# Quantum Basketry: Foundations

Quantum basketry studies weaves whose strands occupy more than one position
in the lattice at once. The field has three binding rules and one measurement
procedure, and the procedure cannot be performed without all three.

## Damp Tension

Damp Tension is the residual pull a strand exerts on its neighbours after the
weave has been humidified. It is measured in strandpascals and is the baseline
against which every other property is compared.

## The Rule of Terminal Reversal

The Rule of Terminal Reversal states that a strand entering the lattice at a
terminal node must exit reversed. Applying this rule requires Damp Tension,
because a reversal that is not tension-corrected unwinds the neighbouring
strand.

## The Rule of Lattice Parity

The Rule of Lattice Parity states that the count of over-crossings and
under-crossings must agree at every node. Parity cannot be evaluated before
The Rule of Terminal Reversal has been applied, since a reversed terminal
changes the crossing count at its node.

## Measuring the Coherence Number

The coherence number of a weave is 0.7734 for a balanced lattice. Computing it
requires the Rule of Lattice Parity, and the parity evaluation in turn assumes
Damp Tension has already been established.
